cohort: The study included 135 neonates diagnosed with necrotizing enterocolitis, categorized into mild and severe NEC groups, and further subdivided by the presence or absence of patent ductus arteriosus.
finding: High-severity patent ductus arteriosus (HsPDA) in neonates is associated with increased severity and progression of necrotizing enterocolitis and significantly impacts multi-system functions including exacerbated respiratory issues, increased left ventricular load, hypercoagulability, disrupted calcium metabolism, and higher risks of sepsis and intraventricular hemorrhage.
